description: We’re a group of students interested in space, science, and technology. We each have different skills and interests, and we want to bring them together to learn, build something creative, and solve a real challenge through NASA Space Apps.
summary:
Our project explores how certain locations on Earth can help us better understand the geological environment of Mars. We developed an interactive research-based website comparing two terrestrial locations, Blue Dragon Flow in idaho usa ,and Axel Heiberg Island in the Canadian Arctic, with the Martian surface.

Through geological research, scientific images, and publicly available NASA and Canadian Space Agency resources, we examined similarities and differences in mineralogy, volcanic formations, terrain, temperature, ice, and environmental conditions. Our goal is to show how studying these Earth environments can provide valuable insights into geological processes that may also occur on Mars.

This project is important because Earth-based analogues allow scientists to investigate Martian-like environments using real observations and accessible data. By bringing these comparisons together in one platform, we hope to make planetary science more understandable and contribute to the broader preparation for future Mars exploration.
details:
1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

Our project is about exploring Earth locations that can help us better understand Mars. We wanted to investigate how some environments on our own planet share geological and environmental characteristics with the Red Planet.

We focused on two locations: Blue Dragon Flow in Hawaii and Axel Heiberg Island in Canada. Although they are very different environments, each offers interesting similarities to certain aspects of Mars.

Blue Dragon Flow allows us to explore basaltic volcanic formations and mineralogical similarities, while Axel Heiberg provides an opportunity to study cold environments, permafrost, ice, and processes that can help us understand Martian polar regions.

We collected information from scientific publications, NASA resources, and satellite data, then organized our findings into a website where visitors can explore the locations and understand their connections to Mars.

2. What benefits does it have?

We believe that studying Mars does not always mean looking directly at Mars. Earth itself contains environments that can help us understand some of the geological processes and conditions found on other planets.

Our project makes these connections easier to discover. It brings together scientific information in one place and helps people understand why certain locations on Earth are interesting for planetary research.

It can also encourage students and other space enthusiasts to become more interested in geology, astronomy, and future space exploration.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

Our main goal is to show how studying different environments on Earth can contribute to our understanding of Mars.

We want to demonstrate that different locations can provide different pieces of the puzzle. Blue Dragon Flow and Axel Heiberg cannot represent Mars as a whole, but they can help us investigate particular geological and environmental characteristics.

We hope our project makes planetary science more accessible and encourages people to look at Earth not only as our home, but also as a valuable place for learning about other worlds.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Since our project focuses mainly on scientific research and comparison, we concentrated on finding reliable information and presenting it clearly.

We used:

  • NASA and NASA/JPL resources for information about Mars.
  • Canadian Space Agency resources and satellite data platforms.
  • Scientific publications and geological research.
  • RADARSAT and RCM data resources to explore Earth-observation possibilities.
  • A computer and internet access for research and website development.
  • Digital tools to organize our research and build our website.

Our approach did not require complex programming or specialized scientific equipment. Instead, we focused on research, comparing scientific information, and communicating our findings through a digital platform.

5. How is your project creative?

What makes our project interesting is the idea of connecting two very different places on Earth to help explain another planet.

Instead of focusing on just one Mars analogue, we chose two locations with different characteristics. One gives us a chance to explore volcanic geology, while the other helps us investigate cold environments and ice-related processes.

We wanted to bring these ideas together in a way that is not only scientifically interesting but also easy for others to explore and understand.

Our website is our way of turning different scientific sources and research findings into one connected experience.

6. What factors did your team consider?

When choosing our locations, we wanted to make sure they were scientifically relevant and offered something different.

We considered:

  • Geological characteristics and surface materials.
  • Mineralogical similarities between Earth and Mars.
  • Temperature, ice, permafrost, and extreme environmental conditions.
  • Terrain, volcanic formations, and other surface features.
  • The availability of reliable scientific information and satellite data.
  • How each location could contribute to understanding a different aspect of Mars.

We also considered our team's experience and available resources, choosing an approach that allowed us to conduct meaningful research and present it using tools accessible to us.

In the end, we selected Blue Dragon Flow and Axel Heiberg because we felt their different characteristics could complement each other and offer two interesting perspectives on Mars.
